reports.title: Barry Preston
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The quality of the documentation was not always of a good standard and part of the reason why his catheter was incorrectly believed to be a long term catheter.
The inquest heard that he was kept on wards that were not suitable for him or his needs. The inquest was told that this was due to capacity and flow issues within the Royal Bolton Hospital.

The inquest heard that whilst he was being treated in acute settings there was no coordination or ownership of his care. It was unclear as to who was making decisions and assessing suitability of placement.
The inquest heard that whilst an in-patient he was served a pudding that was so hot that, while eating it unsupervised, he dropped it on himself and suffered a burn. The
His placement at Laburnum Lodge was made without a clear understanding of his needs. He fell twice within 24 hours sustaining a further bleed to his brain and readmission to the acute hospital.
